hero.headline: Social Security retirement fund projected to run dry in 2032 without congressional action
hero.body:
The Social Security retirement trust fund is now projected to deplete its reserves by 2032, one year earlier than previously forecast, according to a new report. Without intervention from Congress, the program will only be able to pay a portion of scheduled benefits once the fund runs out.

The accelerated timeline for the trust fund shortfall reflects updated projections about the program's financial health. When the retirement fund is exhausted, incoming payroll tax revenue would only cover a percentage of promised benefits, forcing automatic cuts unless lawmakers act to shore up the system. The report highlights the urgency of addressing Social Security's long-term financing challenges.

The Social Security system relies on trust funds that collect payroll taxes from current workers to pay benefits to retirees. The retirement trust fund has been drawing down its reserves as the baby boomer generation reaches retirement age, increasing the number of beneficiaries relative to contributing workers. The updated projection moves the depletion date closer, narrowing the window for potential legislative solutions.

Congress faces difficult choices to stabilize the program. Options include raising payroll taxes, reducing benefits, increasing the retirement age, or some combination of measures. The political sensitivity of Social Security reform has historically made bipartisan agreement difficult, even as actuaries and policy experts have warned about the program's financial trajectory for years.

The report underscores the scale of the challenge facing federal policymakers. Social Security provides essential income for tens of millions of retired Americans, making any reduction in benefits a significant economic and political concern. The 2032 deadline gives lawmakers a defined timeframe to develop and implement reforms before the trust fund reaches critical low levels and automatic benefit cuts would take effect.

cards.headline: U.S. Launches Strikes on Iran After Helicopter Downed Over Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States military carried out strikes against Iranian targets after an Apache helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz, according to military officials. President Donald Trump blamed Iran for the incident and confirmed that the U.S. military would respond.

Central Command directed the military to launch strikes beginning at 10 p.m. UK time on Tuesday. U.S. media reports indicate the strikes targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz. Trump stated on his Truth Social platform that Iran was responsible for the crash and that Washington could not allow such an event to go unanswered. However, a U.S. official told the Associated Press that the helicopter went down after colliding with an Iranian drone, though it remained unclear whether the collision was intentional.

Central Command described the military response as "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded on social media, saying Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered. Leave our region if you want to be safe."

The two Apache crew members were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat, marking the first known drone rescue at sea by the U.S. military. The 24-foot vessel, called a Corsair, located the aviators after they spent approximately two hours in the water. Trump later downplayed the incident in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, saying the helicopter downing "wasn't a big deal" and that the pilot was fine.

The incident came during what officials had described as a fragile ceasefire between the two countries announced in April. The exchange of fire tests the stability of that arrangement and adds to existing tensions in the region. This confrontation follows recent exchanges between Iran and Israel, which included significant military strikes.

Before the helicopter incident, Trump had expressed renewed optimism about negotiations with Iran, stating there was "a good chance" of signing a deal within "two or three days." He suggested that avoiding further bombing would prevent casualties and keep shipping lanes open. Vice President JD Vance indicated the U.S.-Israel war on Iran could conclude within weeks or months.

Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf responded to the escalation by stating, "We prefer the language of diplomacy, but we speak other languages far more fluently. Break your commitments, and we'll switch to what we speak best."

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a vital passage for global oil shipments. Neither country has provided comprehensive details about casualties or the full extent of damage from the strikes. The confrontation presents both governments with decisions about how to respond without triggering a broader conflict.

cards.headline: Earthquake in Philippines Leaves Many Trapped Under Rubble
cards.teaser: Families search for loved ones after the most powerful earthquake to hit the Philippines in 50 years.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 37 people and injuring hundreds. The quake hit approximately 20 kilometers off the coast of Sarangani province, collapsing buildings across the region. The tremors were felt strongly throughout Mindanao and as far away as Manado in Indonesia, triggering tsunami alerts.

Authorities warned people against entering damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks. Families and rescue workers have been working to recover survivors from the rubble in the aftermath of the disaster.

cards.headline: Stock futures decline after U.S. strikes Iran
cards.teaser: Stock futures fell following U.S. military action against Iran in what officials described as self-defense strikes.
cards.body:
Stock futures declined as the U.S. launched military strikes against Iran in response to Iran shooting down a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump confirmed the incident and said the U.S. must respond. Two Army aviators were rescued after the helicopter went down.

Asian stock markets fell following the Middle East developments, while oil prices rose amid concerns about potential supply disruptions in a region critical to global energy supplies. The market moves reflected investor concerns about escalating geopolitical tensions.

cards.headline: UK and Allies Impose Sanctions Over West Bank Settler Violence
cards.teaser: France will bar Israeli Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entry as part of coordinated measures.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom and allied nations, including Australia, have announced sanctions targeting networks that facilitate settler violence in the West Bank. France will deny entry to Israeli far-right Minister Bezalel Smotrich as part of the coordinated action.

Israel has condemned the measures as "disgraceful." The sanctions represent a joint effort by multiple Western governments to address violence in the occupied territory.

cards.headline: NASA names four astronauts for Artemis III lunar mission training
cards.body:
NASA has announced the crew for its Artemis III mission, revealing an all-male team of four astronauts selected to advance the agency's plan to return humans to the Moon. The announcement was made at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston on Tuesday.

Commander Randy Bresnik will lead the crew, joined by European Space Agency pilot Luca Parmitano and NASA mission specialists Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas. The team is scheduled to launch in 2027 for a two-week mission in low Earth orbit.

Unlike previous Artemis missions, the Artemis III crew will not travel to the Moon or approach it closely. Instead, they will remain near Earth to test docking procedures and life support systems for two competing lunar landers: Blue Origin's Blue Moon and SpaceX's Human Landing System. These tests will prepare systems for Artemis IV, the planned first crewed lunar landing since 1972, currently targeted for 2028.

Bresnik brings extensive spaceflight experience to the mission. The Marine colonel previously commanded the International Space Station and flew on Space Shuttle missions. He holds the distinction of being one of only two NASA astronauts to have a child born while in space.

Parmitano, an Italian Air Force fighter pilot, survived a harrowing incident during a 2013 spacewalk when his helmet filled with liquid. He has also earned recognition as the first disc jockey to broadcast from space, and an asteroid bears his name.

Rubio, an Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot and flight surgeon, holds the NASA record for the longest single spaceflight duration at 371 days. He is based in Miami, Florida.

Douglas, a systems engineer and Coast Guard reserve officer, comes from Miami as well. He has not previously flown to space but trained as part of the backup crew alongside Artemis II astronauts during their preparation.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman praised the crew and the broader space program, describing it as "Earth's first starfleet." He highlighted the multiple spacecraft that will operate simultaneously during these missions, including vehicles from the United States, Russia, and China, calling it "the very beginning of Earth's first Starfleet."

The Artemis III mission depends on successful completion of ongoing development work by private contractors. Blue Origin recently experienced a setback when its New Glenn rocket was destroyed in a launchpad explosion on May 28 in Florida. Company officials have expressed confidence that both the rocket and launchpad will be ready for the 2027 flight, with NASA pledging active support to resolve technical challenges.

The mission represents a significant step forward in NASA's long-term strategy to establish sustained lunar exploration and eventually support missions to Mars.

cards.headline: Technology stocks rebound after midday sell-off erases nearly $1 trillion in value
cards.teaser: Wall Street recovered from a sharp decline in technology stocks that briefly wiped out close to $1 trillion in market value.
cards.body:
Technology stocks experienced sharp volatility on Wall Street, with a midday sell-off temporarily wiping out nearly $1 trillion in market value from the sector. Concerns about Federal Reserve monetary policy and valuations in artificial intelligence stocks fueled the decline.

The market reversed course as the session continued, with tech shares recovering their losses. During the downturn, investors rotated into defensive sectors like consumer staples before returning to technology stocks.

cards.headline: Man Arrested After Knife Attack in Belfast Sparks Violence
cards.teaser: A 30-year-old Sudanese man was charged following an assault that was recorded and spread online.
cards.body:
Police in Belfast arrested and charged a 30-year-old Sudanese man following a knife attack on another man. The assault was recorded on video and quickly spread across social media.

The incident sparked widespread disorder in the city, with protesters setting vehicles and homes on fire. The violence has prompted discussions about far-right demonstrations in Northern Ireland, with analysts noting it as a trigger event for anti-immigration protests.

cards.headline: Myanmar Rebels Lose Ground as Military Forces Conscription
cards.teaser: Military forces are pressing men into army service as rebel groups face setbacks on the battlefield.
cards.body:
The BBC's Quentin Sommerville traveled to Myanmar without government permission to document the conflict firsthand. He spent time with rebel fighters at frontline positions to observe how the civil war is developing.

Rebel forces are losing territory to government military units that have intensified conscription efforts, forcing men into army service as part of the campaign against opposition groups. The shift in momentum represents a significant change in the trajectory of Myanmar's conflict.

cards.headline: Brussels Challenges Albania Over Kushner Resort Project
cards.teaser: A luxury resort linked to Jared Kushner threatens to violate EU environmental regulations.
cards.body:
European Union officials are pressing Albania over a resort development linked to Jared Kushner that could breach EU environmental law. The luxury project has sparked mass protests in the country and raised concerns about Albania's bid to join the European Union.

Albania's leader defended the development in an interview. The project has become a focal point in debates about democracy and environmental protection as the country seeks EU membership.

cards.headline: Major Chipmaker Warns of Possible Price Increases
cards.teaser: TSMC cited rising costs in a rare interview discussing the AI boom and chip geopolitics.
cards.body:
A senior executive at TSMC, the world's largest chipmaker, said the company does not rule out price increases as costs rise. The comments came during a rare interview in which the executive discussed the artificial intelligence boom and the geopolitics of semiconductor manufacturing.

The potential price increases could affect the cost of consumer electronics globally. TSMC plays a central role in the global chip supply chain, manufacturing processors for major technology companies.

hero.headline: UFC Event at White House Restricts Press Access to Company-Approved Credentials
hero.body:
The White House will restrict press access to an upcoming UFC event on its grounds unless the sports organization itself grants credentials to journalists, according to the White House press office. This arrangement represents a significant break from standard protocols at the executive mansion, where the White House Correspondents Association and Secret Service typically control media credentials.

Under this new system, UFC will determine which reporters receive access to cover the fight on White House property. The decision has sparked concerns from media organizations and transparency advocates about whether a private company should control press access at a public government building.

The UFC event will mark the first time a professional mixed martial arts competition takes place at the White House. The organization faces substantial logistical challenges in staging an octagon fight within the constraints of the historic property while meeting safety and technical requirements for professional competition.

To accommodate the event, extensive road closures are planned throughout Washington around the White House complex. Multiple streets will experience traffic disruptions as preparations continue for equipment setup and security measures.

The event has drawn commercial activity as well. A super PAC supporting President Trump announced plans to host a fundraiser the day before the UFC fight, with tickets priced at one million dollars per person.

The press access arrangement has generated attention from news organizations and government watchdogs. Traditionally, White House events allow credentialed members of the press corps to cover activities on the grounds, with the White House and Secret Service maintaining control over security and access decisions rather than outside organizations.

The restricted access policy stands in contrast to established practice at the executive mansion, where media access is typically managed through established institutional channels rather than by external companies hosting events. Press organizations have raised questions about the precedent this could set for future events at the White House.

The UFC's control over credentials means that journalists seeking to cover the event will need approval from the sports organization rather than obtaining standard White House press credentials. This arrangement requires coordination between the UFC, the White House, and the Secret Service regarding security protocols and journalist vetting.

The event comes as the Trump administration has faced ongoing discussions about security protocols at official gatherings. The staging of a major sporting event at the White House represents an unusual use of the presidential residence and its grounds, combining entertainment, security considerations, and questions about media access in ways that previous administrations have not attempted.

The coordination between the private sports organization and the government regarding press credentials underscores the complex logistics involved in hosting such an event at a secure federal location.

cards.headline: Texas Teen Sentenced to 35 Years for Fatal Stabbing at Track Meet
cards.teaser: Karmelo Anthony received a 35-year prison sentence after a jury found him guilty of murder in the stabbing death of a high school student.
cards.body:
A Texas jury found Karmelo Anthony, now 19, guilty of murder in the fatal stabbing of Austin Metcalf. The trial, which lasted one week, concluded with Anthony receiving a 35-year prison sentence.

The case drew national attention due to its racial dimensions. Anthony is Black while Metcalf was white. The jury of 12, along with six alternates, included no Black jurors, a factor that sparked discussion on social media about the trial's racial composition.

cards.headline: Sanders-Backed Progressive Advances to Face Republican Valadao in California Swing District
cards.teaser: Randy Villegas, endorsed by Bernie Sanders, will challenge incumbent Republican David Valadao in a key California House race after advancing from the primary.
cards.body:
Progressive Democrat Randy Villegas secured a spot in the general election runoff against Republican Representative David Valadao in California's 22nd Congressional District. The Sanders-backed candidate's advancement represents a defeat for moderate Democrats who had hoped a centrist would emerge to challenge Valadao in the swing district.

House Democrats reportedly threatened to withhold dues from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee following what Axios characterized as the party's poor showing in California primaries. Villegas will face Valadao, the Republican incumbent, in what is expected to be one of the most competitive House races in the state.

cards.headline: Trump-Endorsed Evette and Wilson Advance to South Carolina Governor Runoff
cards.teaser: Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson will face each other in a Republican runoff for South Carolina governor.
cards.body:
Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson have advanced to a Republican runoff in South Carolina's gubernatorial race. Trump endorsed Evette, while Wilson is a Trump supporter. Both candidates are now positioned to compete for the Republican nomination, with the winner favored in the general election given the state's conservative lean.

Representative Nancy Mace's bid for the Republican nomination ended in defeat. The runoff between Evette and Wilson will determine which candidate represents the Republican party against the Democratic nominee in November's general election.

cards.headline: Graham Platner Wins Maine Democratic Senate Primary to Challenge Collins
cards.teaser: Graham Platner secured the Democratic nomination to face Republican Senator Susan Collins in what is expected to be a closely watched Senate race.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Marine veteran, oyster farmer and progressive activist, won Maine's Democratic Senate primary despite a campaign shadowed by personal controversies. His victory sets up a general election against Republican Senator Susan Collins, a key midterm contest that could influence the Senate's balance of power.

Platner's rise has been remarkable for a candidate who has never held elected office. His chief Democratic rival, Maine Governor Janet Mills, suspended her campaign citing lack of funds. Stephen King announced he voted for Platner in the primary.

cards.headline: Billionaire Tom Steyer Fails to Advance in California Governor Race After $200 Million Campaign
cards.teaser: Tom Steyer's second attempt at elected office ended without making the runoff despite spending over $200 million on his gubernatorial campaign.
cards.body:
Billionaire environmental activist Tom Steyer did not advance to the runoff in California's gubernatorial race, marking the end of his second bid for elected office. Steyer spent more than $200 million on the campaign but failed to secure enough support from California voters to continue.

Political analysts suggested the outcome may demonstrate limits on the effectiveness of self-funded campaigns. Steyer's message as a wealthy candidate criticizing economic inequality did not resonate with enough voters to carry him into the general election runoff.

cards.headline: Disorder Erupts in Belfast After Knife Attack Suspect Charged
cards.teaser: Public unrest forced residents to flee homes and led to suspension of public transportation in Belfast following charges in a knife attack case.
cards.body:
Violence erupted on the streets of Belfast following a knife attack on Monday. A man was charged in connection with the incident, triggering widespread disorder across parts of the city.

The unrest forced residents to leave their homes as the situation escalated. Public transportation services were suspended during the disturbances as authorities worked to restore order and manage the disruption to the city.

cards.headline: General Motors to develop energy storage batteries as electric vehicle sales slow
cards.teaser: GM announced plans to manufacture large-scale energy storage batteries for utilities and data centers as the company diversifies beyond electric vehicles.
cards.body:
General Motors announced plans to develop energy storage battery components for electric utilities, data centers, and other businesses. The company will use sodium-ion battery chemistry for these grid-scale storage systems, which help manage fluctuations in power supply and demand. GM is partnering with Peak Energy to scale the technology.

The move follows a similar strategy to Tesla and comes as GM's electric vehicle sales have slowed. The company is also activating vehicle-to-grid capabilities for its current EV and home energy customers, allowing vehicles to help stabilize the electrical grid as demand from AI data centers grows.

cards.headline: TSMC does not rule out price increases as manufacturing costs rise
cards.teaser: A senior executive at the world's largest chipmaker said the company may raise prices as production costs increase.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world's largest chipmaker, has not ruled out raising prices as manufacturing costs increase. In a rare interview, a senior TSMC executive discussed the challenges facing the semiconductor industry amid the artificial intelligence boom and geopolitical complexities of chip production.

Any price increases from TSMC could ripple across the consumer electronics market, since the company supplies semiconductors to major technology firms globally. The executive's comments highlight how cost pressures in chip manufacturing may ultimately affect pricing for consumers worldwide.

cards.headline: Penn Station to receive $8 billion renovation with new design
cards.teaser: New York's Penn Station will undergo an $8 billion redesign featuring columns and natural sunlight, with renderings unveiled by Amtrak and project partners.
cards.body:
Amtrak, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, and Halmar presented detailed plans for an $8 billion redevelopment of Penn Station in New York. The renovation would add architectural columns and bring natural sunlight into the station, which project leaders described as a world-class redesign.

The project team revealed renderings of the planned transformation, though questions about total cost and funding sources remained unresolved. The station name will include a reference to the Trump administration, which is involved in the federal aspects of the project.

cards.headline: Prediction platform Kalshi to require job disclosure from some users after insider trading concerns
cards.teaser: Kalshi announced new rules requiring certain users to reveal employment details following issues with insider trading on the platform.
cards.body:
The prediction betting platform Kalshi will implement new requirements for some users to disclose job details as part of measures to address insider trading concerns. The platform is adding the rules after identifying issues with users trading on non-public information.

The employment disclosure requirements aim to help the platform identify potential conflicts of interest where users might have access to material non-public information related to prediction markets. Kalshi has grown rapidly as a regulated platform for event-based trading.

cards.headline: Google cuts AI Plus subscription price to $4.99 and doubles storage
cards.teaser: Google reduced the price of its AI Plus subscription plan and increased the included cloud storage.
cards.body:
Google lowered the monthly price of its AI Plus subscription tier to $4.99, making premium artificial intelligence features more affordable. The company also doubled the cloud storage included with the plan, adding value for subscribers who use both AI tools and file storage.

The pricing change positions Google competitively in the growing market for consumer AI subscriptions. Several technology companies now offer paid tiers for advanced AI features, with prices typically ranging from $10 to $20 per month. Google's reduced pricing could pressure competitors to adjust their own subscription costs.

cards.headline: Apple demonstrates upgraded Siri AI capabilities at WWDC 2026
cards.teaser: Apple showcased improvements to Siri's artificial intelligence features during its annual developer conference.
cards.body:
Apple showcased significant improvements to Siri at its Worldwide Developers Conference, emphasizing AI enhancements across the voice assistant. The company introduced new intelligence frameworks and development tools for app creators building on the updated platform.

Apple announced it will leverage Nvidia GPUs through Google Cloud infrastructure to run its advanced AI models, marking a strategic shift in how the company scales its AI capabilities. The move reflects Apple's broader approach to managing infrastructure while expanding its artificial intelligence offerings.

cards.headline: GM develops sodium-ion batteries for data centers and grid storage
cards.teaser: General Motors is creating a new battery chemistry for applications beyond automotive use.
cards.body:
General Motors is developing sodium-ion battery technology for stationary energy storage applications. The batteries are designed for data centers, electrical grid storage, and GM's own manufacturing facilities.

Sodium-ion chemistry represents an alternative approach to lithium-ion batteries for large-scale storage applications. GM's entry into this space reflects growing demand for energy storage solutions driven by artificial intelligence expansion and renewable energy adoption.

cards.headline: Starlink adds $10 monthly hardware fee and raises service prices
cards.teaser: SpaceX's satellite internet service introduced new charges for equipment and increased subscription costs.
cards.body:
Starlink shifted from one-time hardware purchases to a $10 monthly equipment fee for its satellite internet service. The company also raised service prices by $5 to $10 per month depending on the plan. The changes affect both new and existing customers.

Starlink has become SpaceX's largest revenue source as the satellite constellation expands globally. The pricing adjustments could increase monthly revenue while making the initial signup cost lower for new subscribers who previously paid several hundred dollars upfront for equipment. The service provides internet access in areas without traditional broadband infrastructure.

cards.headline: Microsoft patches zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by security researcher
cards.teaser: The company fixed security flaws revealed publicly during an ongoing dispute with a researcher.
cards.body:
Microsoft released patches for zero-day security vulnerabilities disclosed by a researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse. The flaws were made public during a dispute between the researcher and the company. Zero-day vulnerabilities are security holes unknown to the software maker and potentially exploitable by attackers.

Microsoft addressed at least two separate vulnerabilities revealed by the researcher. The fixes came through the company's regular update process. Public disclosure of unpatched security flaws before a fix is available typically increases risk to users, though researchers sometimes choose this approach when they believe a vendor is not responding appropriately to security reports.

cards.headline: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 generates simple video games from text prompts
cards.teaser: The AI company released a tool that creates playable games based on user descriptions.
cards.body:
I need to flag an issue with your original card: the sources provided don't confirm that Claude Fable 5 generates video games from text prompts. 

The sources indicate that Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, described as their most powerful widely available AI. It demonstrates strong performance in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks, with advantages that increase on longer, more complex tasks. The model includes safety guardrails blocking high-risk responses in areas like cybersecurity and biology.

One source mentions the model can "make weirdly fun video games," but doesn't provide details about how this works or confirm it's a primary feature.

I recommend returning the original card text unchanged since the core claim about video game generation from text prompts isn't adequately supported by these sources.

hero.headline: Serena Williams wins doubles match in return to professional tennis after nearly four years
hero.body:
Serena Williams marked her comeback to professional tennis with a victory, defeating third seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Erin Routliffe 7-6 (7-2), 6-2 alongside Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko at Queen's Club in London. The match represented Williams's first competitive outing since stepping away from the sport in 2022, after 1,375 days away from professional play.

The 44-year-old Williams described her return as being about "just having fun" rather than chasing wins. "I don't need to win. I've won more than most people have in their whole lives, so for me it's not important," she said. Williams emphasized that she feels no pressure to prove herself further, having already secured 23 Grand Slam singles titles during her career.

Williams chose Mboko, currently ranked ninth in singles, as her doubles partner after being impressed by her performance at the Canadian Open. She noted that Mboko "reminded me a lot of myself" because of her consistent winning mentality and drive to succeed.

For Mboko, the partnership carries special significance. The 19-year-old was only ten years old when Williams won her last Grand Slam title. "Growing up, Serena has always been my idol," Mboko said. "Seeing someone on TV versus actually talking to them in person is very different. She's really nice and very personable, very relatable."

During the match, Williams demonstrated her competitive instincts remained sharp. At a crucial moment with the score tied at 5-5, 30-30 in the first set, she served a 120mph service winner to secure the hold. The pair won the tight opening set in a tiebreak before dominating the second set.

Williams stressed that her primary motivation for returning involves her family. "It's really about my kids getting to see me play," she explained, referencing her eight-year-old daughter Olympia and two-year-old daughter Adira. She added that the summer timing was perfect since her children were not in school.

Regarding her future in tennis, Williams remained noncommittal about returning to singles competition. When asked if she planned to play singles matches, she said: "I can't say yeah, I can't say no. Right now, no." She acknowledged that playing singles would require additional training. Williams has committed to playing doubles in Berlin after Queen's, but her plans beyond that remain uncertain.

Emma Raducanu, who faced Williams in 2022 during what was then her final professional match, expressed enthusiasm about the comeback. "It's really great to see her back," Raducanu said. "She's the greatest female tennis player of all time."

The victory sets up a second-round match for Williams and Mboko as they continue their campaign at Queen's Club, the traditional grass-court warmup tournament before Wimbledon.

cards.headline: World Cup players and officials detained or denied entry to United States
cards.teaser: Multiple World Cup participants have been detained or barred from entering the United States ahead of the tournament.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a Somali referee selected to officiate at the World Cup, was denied entry into the United States. The decision prevented him from fulfilling what he described as a dream opportunity, with historical precedent suggesting he may not receive another chance to officiate at a World Cup.

Multiple World Cup players and officials have faced detention or entry denials while attempting to arrive in the United States for the tournament. The White House World Cup chief defended the visa restrictions, which included the Somali referee and Iranian nationals.

cards.headline: Marco Silva agrees to replace Jose Mourinho as Benfica head coach
cards.teaser: Marco Silva has agreed to become Benfica's new head coach following Jose Mourinho's departure for Real Madrid.
cards.body:
Portuguese club Benfica has confirmed Marco Silva as its new head coach following Jose Mourinho's departure to Real Madrid. Silva will now lead the club in domestic and European competitions.

The coaching appointment comes as Benfica formalizes Mourinho's move to the Spanish giants. Silva takes charge of a squad competing at the highest level of Portuguese football.

cards.headline: Big 12 athletic directors hold emergency call over Brendan Sorsby eligibility ruling
cards.teaser: Big 12 athletic directors convened to discuss the court decision that restored Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's NCAA eligibility.
cards.body:
Big 12 athletic directors and the conference commissioner held a call to discuss the fallout from a court ruling that restored Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's eligibility after the NCAA had denied it. The emergency meeting came as Georgia and Nebraska announced they would boycott future games against Texas Tech in response to the decision.

A court overturned the NCAA's denial of Sorsby's eligibility, creating a dispute about the governing body's authority over player eligibility decisions. The Big 12 and Big Ten conferences are considering potential actions in response to the ruling. The situation has sparked debate about whether the decision protects a player who faced health challenges or undermines the NCAA's regulatory framework.

cards.headline: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reports to mandatory minicamp amid contract talks
cards.teaser: Christian Gonzalez attended the first day of Patriots mandatory minicamp while discussions continue about his contract situation.
cards.body:
New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reported to mandatory minicamp and participated in the first day of activities. Gonzalez reiterated his commitment to the Patriots organization despite ongoing contract negotiations, stating he wants to remain with the team.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and Gonzalez both addressed the contract discussions publicly during minicamp. Wide receiver A.J. Brown stood out during the first day of practice activities. Gonzalez's presence at the mandatory minicamp satisfied team requirements as he and the organization work through the contract situation.

cards.headline: England beats Ukraine but misses automatic World Cup qualification
cards.teaser: England defeated Ukraine 3-0 but failed to secure automatic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
cards.body:
England's women's national team defeated Ukraine 3-0 with goals from Carter, Stanway, and Mead, but the victory did not secure automatic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup. Spain's 6-1 win over Iceland on the same day meant England finished second in their group with 15 points, missing out on an automatic spot.

England's failure to qualify automatically stems from their inferior head-to-head record against Spain following a 4-0 loss in Mallorca earlier in the week. The Lionesses will now compete in the playoff round to reach the tournament in Brazil. Manager Sarina Wiegman expressed confidence that England will still qualify despite having to navigate the additional playoff stage.

cards.headline: Hurricanes scratch Frederik Andersen, start Brandon Bussi in Stanley Cup Final Game 4
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes made a goaltending change for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final against the Vegas Golden Knights.
cards.body:
Carolina Hurricanes head coach Rod Brind'Amour scratched goaltender Frederik Andersen and chose to start Brandon Bussi for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final in Las Vegas. Brind'Amour had kept the goaltending decision private before the game as the Hurricanes tried to keep pace with the Golden Knights in the series.

The Stanley Cup Final has been closely contested, with Game 4 representing a pivotal moment in the series. The Hurricanes needed a strong performance from Bussi to remain competitive against Vegas. The goaltending change suggested the coaching staff sought a different approach after the previous games in the series.

hero.headline: Art Directors Guild Condemns Martin Scorsese Over AI Partnership
hero.body:
Martin Scorsese has drawn sharp criticism from industry professionals after revealing he has invested in and partnered with Black Forest Labs, a German artificial intelligence company specializing in text-to-image generation technology.

The acclaimed director, appointed as partner and adviser to the company in 2025, announced that he is using AI tools to create storyboards for his films. In a statement, Scorsese explained his reasoning: "I'm interested in the intersection of technology and storytelling, and seeing how that can push the bounds of creativity to create deeper and richer experiences for audiences."

He emphasized that cinema is still a young medium and should remain open to evolution. Scorsese noted that for seven decades he has been creating his own storyboards and has long struggled with how to effectively communicate his visual ideas to cast and crew members. "Now with this tool, I can share what I'm visualising more clearly and efficiently to my creative team," he said. He added that testing the technology on a scene proved "creatively freeing" and allowed faster movement through preproduction without sacrificing quality.

The announcement sparked immediate backlash from storyboard and concept artists. Karla Ortiz, a concept artist who worked on multiple Marvel films including Black Panther and Avengers: Endgame, responded angrily on social media, stating: "He throws every single storyboard artist he's ever worked with under the bus. To use his legacy and power for this is just so disgusting."

Samuel Deats, director of the animated series Castlevania, also criticized the partnership: "There is absolutely no reason to need AI built on the stolen work of millions of artists to storyboard your vision, have some damn pride and respect your peers."

The Art Directors Guild released a formal statement on social media condemning Scorsese's decision, accusing him of abandoning the human artists who have been instrumental throughout his career in creating his most iconic films. The guild represents art directors and production designers working across film, television, and other visual media.

Scorsese's move places him among a growing number of prominent filmmakers embracing AI technology. Director Steven Soderbergh used AI-generated sequences in his recent documentary John Lennon: The Last Interview, while Jurassic World Rebirth director Gareth Edwards has praised AI as helpful to his work. Jane Rosenthal, co-founder of the Tribeca film festival, defended screening Dreams of Violets, a fully AI-generated film about protesters in Iran.

The partnership reflects broader tensions in the entertainment industry over artificial intelligence's role in creative work, with concerns mounting about its impact on employment and artistic integrity among writers, actors, and visual artists.

cards.headline: Nick Reiner Seeks Trust Funds for Legal Defense in Parents' Murder Case
cards.teaser: Nick Reiner has petitioned a Los Angeles probate court to access trust funds established by his parents to pay for his legal defense in their murder case.
cards.body:
Nick Reiner, son of Rob and Michele Reiner, filed a petition in Los Angeles probate court seeking release of trust funds to pay for his legal defense. His attorneys argue he should be able to access a trust that was set up by his parents shortly after his birth.

The petition comes as Reiner faces charges in connection with the murders of his parents. The trust in question was established by Rob and Michele Reiner as part of their estate planning. Reiner's legal team is asking the court to allow him to use these funds to cover the costs of his criminal defense.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Appears at Toy Story 5 Premiere
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift made a surprise appearance at the world premiere of Toy Story 5 at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift made a surprise appearance at the world premiere of Toy Story 5 at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles on Tuesday night. While she skipped the step and repeat photo line, Swift participated in a large cast photo with other attendees.

Swift's presence at the event coincided with her contribution to the film's soundtrack, marking her involvement with the animated sequel's release.

cards.headline: Jay-Z and Eminem Reunite on Rakim Album
cards.teaser: Jay-Z and Eminem will appear together on a track for Rakim's collaborative album, marking their first collaboration in 25 years.
cards.body:
The two rap stars are reuniting for a track on Rakim's upcoming collaborative album with Kurupt and Masta Killa. The song represents the first time Jay-Z and Eminem have worked together in a quarter century.

The collaboration pays homage to Rakim, a foundational figure in hip-hop history. The album brings together multiple generations of rap artists, with Jay-Z and Eminem joining fellow rap icon Rakim alongside Kurupt and Masta Killa for the project.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV Meets Bad Bunny in Spain
cards.teaser: Puerto Rican singer Bad Bunny and his family met with Pope Leo XIV during a visit to Spain.
cards.body:
Bad Bunny met Pope Leo XIV in Spain. The Puerto Rican artist was accompanied by his family during the meeting with the pontiff.

The encounter took place as Bad Bunny continues his international presence as one of the leading figures in Latin music. Pope Leo XIV has met with various cultural figures and artists during his papacy.

cards.headline: Persimmon Acquires Mystery Film Death on the Brandywine
cards.teaser: Independent distributor Persimmon has acquired U.S. and international distribution rights to the mystery film Death on the Brandywine starring Kate Burton.
cards.body:
Persimmon has secured distribution rights for the U.S. and several international territories for the mystery film Death on the Brandywine. The film stars Kate Burton, known for her work on Grey's Anatomy, alongside Rena Sofer, Tuc Watkins, Jay Huguley, Walt Willey, Shanley Caswell, and Guy Nardulli.

The cast includes actors from various television series including 24, Paradise, Cape Fear, All My Children, NCIS: New Orleans, and Tulsa King. The independent distribution company will handle the film's release in multiple markets.

cards.headline: Craig Ferguson Says He's Glad He Left Late Night Before Trump Presidency
cards.teaser: Former Late Late Show host Craig Ferguson said he was relieved to have ended his show before Donald Trump became president.
cards.body:
Craig Ferguson, who hosted CBS's "The Late Late Show," recently told Obsessed: The Podcast that he was relieved to have exited late-night television before Donald Trump's presidency began. Ferguson departed the program before having to navigate the political landscape that followed.

The former host acknowledged uncertainty about how he would have handled covering Trump as president, expressing gratitude that he avoided facing that particular challenge during his tenure in late-night hosting.

hero.headline: Evette and Wilson advance to runoff in South Carolina governor's race
hero.teaser: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson will compete in a GOP runoff after neither won a majority in the South Carolina primary.
hero.body:
Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson will face each other in a runoff for the Republican gubernatorial nomination in South Carolina after neither secured enough votes to win outright in Tuesday's primary.

Evette, who leads in fundraising with approximately 3.5 million dollars including 1 million of her own money, received Trump's endorsement ahead of the primary. Wilson, who has served as attorney general since 2011 and holds the rank of reserve colonel in the National Guard's judge advocate general corps, is also a Trump supporter but did not receive the former president's formal backing.

The result represents a significant loss for U.S. Representative Nancy Mace, who finished fifth in the crowded Republican field. Mace attributed her defeat to her vote in favor of releasing the Epstein files, a position that drew criticism from Trump supporters. "I voted to release the Epstein files and lost some support for that," she said in a statement. "As a survivor, I chose to stand on principle and stand against the Epstein cover-up."

Evette, an entrepreneur who built Quality Business Solutions into a billion-dollar revenue company before entering politics, was selected as the running mate for outgoing Governor Henry McMaster in 2018. Wilson is the adoptive son of longtime Republican U.S. Representative Joe Wilson.

Two other candidates, U.S. Representative Ralph Norman and Rom Reddy, were also defeated in the primary. Norman, described as one of the most conservative members of the House, trailed the top two finishers. Reddy, a former ExxonMobil executive and child of immigrants, entered the race with 5 million dollars of his own money, partly motivated by frustrations over a lengthy dispute with environmental regulators regarding a seawall at his Sea Island property.

The winner of the Republican runoff will face Democrat Jermaine Johnson, a state representative and former professional basketball player from a Columbia-area district, in the general election. Johnson won broad endorsement from Democratic party officials before securing his party's nomination on Tuesday.

South Carolina changed its election process in 2012 so that the governor and lieutenant governor run as a ticket in general elections. Given the state's conservative lean, the Republican nominee is considered the favorite for the general election, though Democrats hope to gain ground across the ballot.

In another closely watched South Carolina contest, Republican Senator Lindsey Graham secured his party's nomination after facing five challengers, the most he has encountered since taking office in 2003. Graham will face Democrat and pediatrician Annie Andrews in November's general election.

cards.headline: Trump moves up Pulte's appointment as acting intelligence chief
cards.teaser: President Trump announced Bill Pulte will assume the acting Director of National Intelligence role earlier than planned, despite opposition to the controversial nomination.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Tuesday that Bill Pulte will assume the role of acting Director of National Intelligence sooner than originally planned. The accelerated timeline comes as Congress races to reauthorize Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act before it expires at the end of the week.

The nomination has triggered significant backlash among lawmakers concerned about the surveillance law's renewal. Trump met with House Speaker Mike Johnson at the White House on Tuesday as pressure mounts on the president to nominate a permanent intelligence director instead, a move some Republicans believe is necessary to save the controversial surveillance authority.

cards.headline: U.S. launches strikes on Iranian air defenses after helicopter downing
cards.teaser: The United States launched strikes against Iranian air defense and radar systems near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, beginning at 5pm Eastern Time.
cards.body:
The United States launched strikes against Iranian air defense and radar systems near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening at 5pm Eastern Time, according to U.S. Central Command. The operation was in response to Iran's downing of a U.S. helicopter. President Trump had earlier accused Iran of the attack and vowed to respond.

The strikes targeted infrastructure around the strategic waterway through which much of the world's oil passes. Bahrain's king said his country's air defenses repelled Iranian attacks, suggesting Iran responded to the U.S. operation. The exchange underscores rising tensions between Washington and Tehran, complicating efforts toward potential diplomatic negotiations.

cards.headline: Navy admiral fired by Hegseth heads to runoff for South Carolina House seat
cards.teaser: Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral dismissed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, will face veteran Mac Deford in a Democratic primary runoff.
cards.body:
Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year, advanced to a runoff in the Democratic primary for South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. She will face veteran Mac Deford in the next round, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Lacore and Deford defeated several other Democrats competing for the nomination in the district, which runs along the state's southeast coast. The winner will compete for the seat currently held by Rep. Nancy Mace.

cards.headline: Former Republican Kiley to face Democratic challenger in California House race
cards.teaser: Rep. Kevin Kiley, who switched from Republican to independent, will compete against Democrat Richard Pan in November, Decision Desk HQ projects.
cards.body:
Rep. Kevin Kiley, a former Republican now running as an independent, advanced to the general election and will face Democrat Richard Pan in November. Decision Desk HQ made the projection Tuesday evening.

Kiley garnered 24.53 percent of the vote while Pan, a doctor and small business owner, received 23.21 percent. Under California's top-two primary system, both candidates advanced regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Platner advances to face Collins in Maine Senate race
cards.teaser: Progressive oyster farmer Graham Platner won the Democratic primary and will challenge Republican Sen. Susan Collins this fall despite recent controversies.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, won Maine's Democratic Senate primary despite a campaign marked by personal controversies. The progressive newcomer will face Republican Sen. Susan Collins in the fall.

Collins ran unopposed in the Republican primary and is seeking her sixth term. The incumbent has served in the Senate since 1997 and is known as one of the chamber's more moderate Republicans.

cards.headline: Becerra and Hilton to compete in California governor's race
cards.teaser: Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton advanced to November's gubernatorial election after a week of vote counting in California's primary.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra will compete in California's November gubernatorial election. With 91 percent of votes counted, Becerra led with 27.9 percent support to Hilton's 25 percent.

Hilton held an early advantage on election night but saw his lead narrow as California's vote counting process continued over the following week. He secured the second-place finish needed to advance under the state's top-two primary system.
